mainTopic: The perforated pot (גט on a leaf, קנין, border of ארץ ישראל) and the three stages of hide for writing a גט
overview: This amud opens by finishing the argument about a גט written on a leaf growing in a perforated pot (עציץ נקוב). אביי says it is valid because the whole pot can be handed over. רבא says it is invalid, by גזירה, in case the husband cuts the leaf off. The גמרא then teaches the rules of קנין for such a pot. The plants count like land and the pot is movable, so חזקה on the plants also acquires the pot, but חזקה on the pot alone acquires nothing. Next, אביי and רבא argue whether a pot on the border of ארץ ישראל follows its hole or its branches. The גמרא limits their argument to a plant that has not rooted, and defends this against challenges from the terraced gardens and from a tree growing across the border. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה. עולא defines three stages of hide (מצה, חיפה, דיפתרא), each with its own size for carrying on שבת. The amud ends by asking who the חכמים are who validate such a גט, and רבי אלעזר's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the leaf-in-pot גט can be valid
steps.stepSummary: The end of אביי's reasoning: the husband can pick up the whole pot, leaf and all, and hand it to his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he can take it and give it to her.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of אביי's opinion from the previous lines. He explains why a גט written on a leaf in a perforated pot is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry with a גט written on something still growing is that it would have to be cut off before it is given. אביי says no cutting is needed here, because the husband can hand over the whole pot with the leaf still attached. So the גט is complete when it is given, exactly as written.

keyTerms.meaning: a pot with a hole in it, so its plants count as attached to the ground

steps.confusionAlert: The leaf is not cut off and handed over by itself. אביי means the whole pot is handed over with the leaf still growing in it.

phrases.english: because he takes it
and gives it to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's opinion, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט on a leaf in a perforated pot is valid, since the whole pot can be handed over without cutting anything.

steps.title: רבא: invalid, because he might cut the leaf off
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees and calls the גט invalid. This is a rabbinic decree, made because the husband might cut off the leaf and hand over only that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is invalid. This is a decree, in case he cuts it off.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite ruling from אביי. He says the גט is invalid because of a protective decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not say handing over the whole pot fails. His concern is that a husband might cut the leaf off and give her only the leaf, and that would make the גט invalid. To prevent this, the רבנן ruled out the whole setup.

keyTerms.meaning: a protective decree made by the רבנן

steps.whatToRemember: אביי says the גט is valid, since he can hand over the whole pot. רבא says it is invalid, through a גזירה, in case he cuts the leaf off.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a גזירה works. Something that would be fine on its own can be forbidden to stop people from making a related mistake.

phrases.english: Rava says: it is invalid,
a decree, lest he cut it off.
phrases.notes: He means the husband might cut the leaf off the plant and give her just the leaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An opposing opinion to אביי's ruling in Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גט is invalid by rabbinic decree, in case he cuts off the leaf and gives it alone.

steps.title: Pot belongs to one person, plants to another
steps.stepSummary: If the pot owner sells the pot to the plant owner, pulling the pot (משיכה) is enough. If the plant owner sells the plants to the pot owner, the buyer must take חזקה of the plants.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pot belongs to one person and the plants in it belong to another. If the pot owner sells to the plant owner, the buyer acquires as soon as he pulls the pot. If the plant owner sells to the pot owner, the buyer does not acquire until he takes possession of the plants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about the perforated pot, this time about buying and selling it. It sets out two cases where the pot and the plants have different owners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pot is a movable object (מטלטלין), so it can be acquired by משיכה, pulling it. The plants in a perforated pot count as attached to the ground, like קרקע, so pulling does not work for them. The buyer must do an act of חזקה on the plants themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: plants or seeds growing in the pot
pulled (משיכה, the way movable things are acquired)
takes possession through an act of חזקה, the way land is acquired

phrases.english: A pot belonging to one person
and plants belonging to another;
if the pot owner sold to the plant owner,
once he pulled it, he acquired it.
If the plant owner sold to the pot owner,
he does not acquire until he takes possession of the plants.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָצִיץ שֶׁל אֶחָד וּזְרָעִים שֶׁל אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the גט question to a new topic about the same perforated pot: how it is bought and sold.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pot is acquired by משיכה. The plants, which count as land, are acquired only by חזקה.

steps.title: One owner sells both: חזקה on the plants gets the pot too
steps.stepSummary: When one person sells both the pot and the plants, the buyer's חזקה on the plants also gives him the pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the pot and plants belong to one person and he sells them to another, once the buyer takes possession of the plants, he has acquired the pot too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third case, where one owner sells both items together. Doing חזקה on the plants is enough to acquire the pot along with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plants count as land and the pot is movable. When both are sold together, acquiring the land part carries the movable part along with it. No separate משיכה of the pot is needed.

phrases.english: A pot and plants belonging to one person,
and he sold them to another;
if he took possession of the plants, he acquired the pot.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָצִיץ וּזְרָעִים שֶׁל אֶחָד וּמְכָרָן לְאַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third case to the two cases in Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both are sold together, חזקה on the plants also acquires the pot.

steps.title: This matches the משנה about movables acquired along with land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects the rule in Step 4 to the משנה in קידושין: movable property can be acquired along with land through money, a document, or חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what we learned: property that has no guarantee can be acquired together with property that has a guarantee, through money, a document, or taking possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the rule of Step 4 is one example of a known משנה. It names the general principle behind the pot case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Property with a guarantee" is land, because a creditor can collect from it. "Property without a guarantee" is movable items. The משנה teaches that movables can be acquired together with land, which is exactly what happens when חזקה on the plants (land) also gets the pot (movable).

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what we learned (pointing to an earlier source)
a guarantee, meaning land that a creditor can collect from
money, a document, taking possession: the three ways to acquire land

steps.confusionAlert: "Without a guarantee" does not mean the item is worse. It is simply the term for movable property, since a creditor cannot rely on it the way he relies on land.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, קנין אגב, is a basic tool in the laws of buying and selling across all of ש״ס.

phrases.english: And this is what we learned:
phrases.notes: This refers to a משנה in קידושין (26a).

phrases.english: property that has no guarantee

phrases.aramaic: נִקְנִין עִם נְכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן אַחְרָיוּת –
phrases.english: is acquired together with property that has a guarantee,
through money, a document, or taking possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and general principle behind Step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that חזקה on the plants also acquires the pot.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in קידושין: movables are acquired along with land through money, a document, or חזקה.

steps.title: חזקה on the pot alone acquires nothing
steps.stepSummary: If the buyer takes חזקה only of the pot, he does not even acquire the pot. He must take חזקה of the plants.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he took possession of the pot, he did not acquire even the pot, until he takes possession of the plants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reverse of Step 4. Doing חזקה on the pot does not work, not even for the pot itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקה is a way to acquire land, not movable things, so it does nothing for the pot by itself. Through חזקה, the pot can only come along with the plants. To get it, the buyer must either pull the pot (משיכה) or take חזקה of the plants.
steps.whatToRemember: Plants in a perforated pot count as land and the pot is movable. חזקה on the plants acquires both. חזקה on the pot acquires nothing. משיכה works for the pot.
steps.confusionAlert: One might think חזקה on the pot should at least acquire the pot. It does not, because חזקה is not a valid way to acquire movable items.

phrases.english: If he took possession of the pot,
he did not acquire even the pot,
until he takes possession of the plants.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶחְזִיק בְּעָצִיץ אַף עָצִיץ לֹא קָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite case of Step 4, finishing the set of cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקה on the pot alone does not acquire even the pot. Only חזקה on the plants carries the pot along.

steps.title: A pot with its hole in ארץ ישראל and its branches outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a perforated pot whose hole is in ארץ ישראל but whose branches extend outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If its hole is in ארץ ישראל and its branches are outside ארץ ישראל, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about the perforated pot from the earlier steps. This sets up the argument between אביי and רבא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pot sits right on the border. Its hole, which connects it to the ground, is on one side and its branches are on the other. The question is which side decides where the plant counts as growing, for example for מצוות that apply only to produce of ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Its hole (the opening in the bottom of the pot)

phrases.english: Its hole is in the Land [of Israel]
and its branches are outside the Land — what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the perforated pot, moving from buying and selling to where the plant counts as growing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the location of the hole or of the branches decide whether the plant counts as growing in ארץ ישראל?

steps.title: אביי follows the hole; רבא follows the branches
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that we go by the hole. רבא rules that we go by the branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We go by its hole. רבא said: We go by its branches.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to the question. אביי looks at where the hole is, and רבא looks at where the branches are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the hole is what connects the plant to the land, so the hole's location decides. For רבא, the place where the plant actually grows out, its branches, decides.

phrases.english: אביי said: We go after its hole.
רבא said: We go after its branches.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: בָּתַר נִקְבּוֹ אָזְלִינַן. רָבָא אָמַר: בָּתַר נוֹפוֹ אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7 with a dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אביי: the hole decides. רבא: the branches decide.

steps.title: The argument is only when the roots stay inside the pot
steps.stepSummary: If the plant's roots grew out into the ground, everyone agrees. They argue only when the roots did not grow out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where it took root, everyone agrees. Where they argue is where it did not take root.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the argument between אביי and רבא. It applies only when the roots are still inside the pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the roots have grown through the hole into the ground, the plant is truly planted there, so everyone agrees where it counts as growing. Only when the roots stay inside the pot is it unclear whether the hole or the branches decide.

keyTerms.meaning: Took root (the roots grew out into the ground)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי and רבא argue about every plant on a border. This step limits their argument to a plant whose roots did not grow out of the pot.

phrases.english: Where it took root, everyone does not disagree.
phrases.notes: He means the roots pushed out through the hole into the actual ground.

phrases.english: When they do disagree — it is where it did not take root.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּדְאַשְׁרוּשׁ, כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְלִיגִי. כִּי פְּלִיגִי – בִּדְלָא אַשְׁרוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the dispute of Step 8 to the case where the roots stayed in the pot.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the plant has rooted into the ground, everyone agrees. The dispute is only about a plant that has not rooted.

steps.title: Challenge from the two terraced gardens
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: don't תנאים argue even about a rooted plant? In the משנה of the two terraced gardens, רבי מאיר gives the vegetables to the upper owner and רבי יהודה gives them to the lower owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where it took root, they do not argue?! But we learned: Two gardens, one above the other, with vegetables growing in between. רבי מאיר says they belong to the upper one. רבי יהודה says they belong to the lower one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 9. It brings a משנה where the vegetables are clearly rooted, yet there is still an argument over whether the roots or the leaves decide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vegetables grow out of the wall between the gardens. Their roots are in the upper garden's soil, but they hang into the lower garden's space. Since רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue here even though the vegetables are rooted, it seems that being rooted does not end the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה (introduces a challenge)
The upper one (owner of the upper garden)
The lower one (owner of the lower garden)

phrases.english: And where it took root, they do not disagree?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: שְׁתֵּי גִּינּוֹת זוֹ עַל גַּב זוֹ,
phrases.english: But didn't we learn: Two gardens, one above the other,
and vegetables between them,
phrases.notes: The vegetables grow out of the wall between the two levels.

phrases.english: רבי מאיר says: They belong to the upper one.
רבי יהודה says: They belong to the lower one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in Step 9 that nobody argues about a rooted plant.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that everyone agrees when the plant has taken root.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the terraced-gardens משנה the vegetables are rooted, yet תנאים still argue whether the upper owner (where the roots are) or the lower owner (where the leaves are) gets them.

steps.title: The gardens case has its own special reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the gardens argument is based on the reason given in that משנה: the upper owner could take away his soil and the vegetables would be gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is as the reason is taught: רבי מאיר said, What if the upper owner wants to take his earth? There would be no vegetables here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The gardens case is not a general argument about roots versus leaves, because that משנה gives its own reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר gives the vegetables to the upper owner because the upper owner controls the soil they need. If he removed his soil, the vegetables would be gone. That is a special reason about who controls the plant, so the gardens argument does not show a general dispute about rooted plants, and Step 9 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: As the reason is taught (in that source itself)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי (follow the hole) and רבא (follow the branches) argue only about a plant whose roots stay inside the pot. The terraced-gardens משנה does not contradict this, because רבי מאיר there relies on a special reason: the upper owner could remove the soil.

phrases.english: There, it is as the reason is taught —
רבי מאיר said:
What if the upper one wants
to take away his earth,
there would be no vegetables here!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10 by showing that the gardens argument rests on a special reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the cited source has its own stated reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The gardens argument seemed to be a general dispute over whether roots or leaves decide, even for a rooted plant.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר's ruling there rests on the upper owner's power to remove the soil, so it says nothing against the claim that everyone agrees about a rooted plant.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's reason in the two-gardens case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the reason from the gardens משנה. רבי יהודה gives the vegetables to the lower owner because he could fill his space with earth and bury them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: What if the lower owner wanted to fill his garden with earth? Then there would be no vegetables here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from step 11 by quoting רבי יהודה's side of the reasoning. The lower owner can wipe out the vegetables too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, רבי מאיר said the upper owner controls the vegetables because he can remove his soil. רבי יהודה answers that the lower owner can bury them with earth. So both sides argue about who controls the vegetables, not about whether roots or branches decide. That is why this משנה does not disagree with step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: The lower one, meaning the owner of the lower garden

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
What if the lower one wants
to fill his garden with earth,
there are no vegetables here!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מָה אִם יִרְצֶה הַתַּחְתּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer in step 11 by giving רבי יהודה's side of the reasoning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason: the gardens argument is about control, not about roots or branches.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The gardens argument seemed to be about rooted plants whose leaves hang over another area.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each owner can destroy the vegetables, so they argue only about who controls them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It removes the gardens משנה as a challenge, so step 9's claim stands for now.

steps.title: Challenge from a tree partly inside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. A ברייתא shows רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל arguing about a rooted tree that is partly inside and partly outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, don't they argue even about a rooted plant? It was taught: A tree that is partly in ארץ ישראל and partly outside it has untithed and non-sacred produce mixed together. That is רבי's view. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: What grows in the obligated area is obligated, and what grows in the exempt area is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to show that תנאים do argue about a plant that is rooted in the ground. That would go against step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said that once a plant is rooted in the ground, everyone agrees. But a tree is rooted in the ground, and רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל still argue about it. רבי treats all the fruit as mixed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל splits the fruit by area.

keyTerms.meaning: And still: a new challenge on the same point
Produce from which תרומות ומעשרות have not yet been taken
Non-sacred produce that needs no tithing

phrases.english: And still, do they not argue where it took root?!
But it was taught:
A tree, part of it in the Land
and part of it outside the Land;
untithed and non-sacred produce are mixed with each other,
These are the words of Rabbi.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
What grows in the obligated place is obligated,
and what grows in the exempt place is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי, בִּדְאַשְׁרוּשׁ לָא פְּלִיגִי?! וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the gardens challenge is answered, the גמרא brings a second challenge to step 9 from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 9: if the roots grew into the ground, everyone agrees.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A tree is rooted, yet תנאים still argue about how to treat its fruit when it crosses the border.

steps.title: Suggesting that the tree's branches are split
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how the ברייתא would fit its challenge. The roots are in one place, but the branches spread across the border.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it talking about a case where some of its branches are in ארץ ישראל and some of its branches are outside it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly how it reads the ברייתא so that it becomes a real challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the roots are all in one place and only the branches cross the border, then the argument is about branches on a rooted tree. That is the same kind of case step 9 said everyone agrees on. That makes the challenge sharp.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it the case that: the גמרא offers a reading that proves its point

phrases.english: Is it not that part of its branches are in the Land
and part of its branches are outside the Land?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge in step 13 by explaining what case the ברייתא must be about.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only the branches are split, then תנאים argue about branches even on a rooted tree.

steps.title: No, the roots are split
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that reading. The ברייתא is about a tree whose roots themselves are partly inside and partly outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Some of the roots are in ארץ ישראל and some of the roots are outside it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the challenge by reading the ברייתא as a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the roots themselves cross the border, then the argument is not about roots against branches. The tree really draws from both places. So step 9 still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is now saying roots don't matter. It is saying the ברייתא's tree has roots in both places, which is why there is anything to argue about.

phrases.english: No; part of the roots are in the Land
and part of the roots are outside the Land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading offered in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that the ברייתא is about split branches.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as a case of split roots, which has nothing to do with step 9.

steps.title: How can רבן שמעון בן גמליאל split the fruit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reasoning. If the roots are mixed, how can we know which fruit came from which side?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the roots are on both sides, the גמרא asks how רבן שמעון בן גמליאל can divide the fruit cleanly into obligated and exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With roots in both places, every fruit seems to draw from both sides. That fits רבי, who says the fruit is mixed. But רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's clean split needs an explanation.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל?
phrases.english: And what is the reason of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the new reading in step 15, which raises a problem for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבן שמעון בן גמליאל can divide the fruit when the roots are in both places.

steps.title: A rock separates the roots
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a rock divides the roots. Each side of the tree feeds only from its own area.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because a rock separates them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's case, a rock splits the roots into two separate groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the rock, we can tell which part of the tree feeds from ארץ ישראל and which part feeds from outside it. So the fruit can be divided. The tree is still rooted on both sides, so step 9 is not contradicted.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about the tree is a case of roots in both places, not of branches crossing over. So step 9 stands: when a plant is rooted, everyone agrees. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל splits the fruit only because a rock divides the roots.

phrases.english: Because a rock separates.
phrases.notes: He means a rock runs between the roots, up to the trunk, keeping each side's roots apart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A rock divides the roots, so each part of the tree is clearly fed from one side only.

steps.title: What is רבי's reasoning?
steps.stepSummary: If a rock divides the roots, why does רבי treat the fruit as mixed?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has just said that a rock divides the roots. Now it asks why רבי still treats the fruit as a mixture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 explained רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who splits the tree by its roots. But if the roots really are divided, רבי's view that everything is mixed needs its own explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, who compiled the משנה

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having explained רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the גמרא now asks about the other side of the debate.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי treats the fruit as mixed even though a rock separates the roots.

steps.title: The roots mix again further up
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that even with divided roots, the sap mixes again inside the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they mix together again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that, according to רבי, the nourishment from both sides mixes together again higher up in the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rock separates the roots only underground. Above that, everything flows into one trunk, so רבי says no fruit can be tied to one side.

phrases.english: Because they go back and mix.
phrases.notes: He means that the roots' nourishment joins together again above the rock, in the body of the tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The separated roots mix together again in the tree, so the fruit is a mixture.

steps.title: What exactly do they disagree about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the underlying principle behind the argument of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that both sides are explained, the גמרא asks what basic idea their argument really depends on. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a rock divides the roots. So the argument must be about what happens above the ground.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on both explanations to find the real point of the argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The core principle that divides רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Does the air mix the tree, or does each side stand alone?
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the part of the tree above ground mixes everything. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says each side of the tree stays separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds that the air mixes it up. The other Sage holds that this side stands alone and that side stands alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the root of the argument: does the tree above ground blend everything together, or does each half stay its own?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, once the tree rises into the air, the two sides blend, so all the fruit is mixed. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the tree is like two separate trees side by side, each fed only from its own land.

keyTerms.meaning: the air (the open space above the ground)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: the air mixes, so all the fruit is mixed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: each side stands alone, so each side's fruit follows its own land.

phrases.english: One Sage holds: the air mixes it up,
and the other Sage holds: this side stands by itself
phrases.notes: This second Sage is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: and that side stands by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 and closes the tree discussion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether the tree above ground blends the two sides or keeps them separate.

steps.title: עולא: there are three kinds of hide
steps.stepSummary: Going back to רבי יהודה בן בתירא in the משנה, עולא lists three stages of leather: מצה, חיפה, and דיפתרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said, 'רבי יהודה בן בתירא says...' רבי חייא בר אסי said in the name of עולא: There are three kinds of hide: מצה, חיפה, and דיפתרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה's opinion of רבי יהודה בן בתירא and brings עולא's list of three stages of hide to explain what 'unfinished leather' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hide goes through several steps before it becomes finished leather. עולא names three of them. The next steps will define each one, starting with מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא in the משנה who rules about what a גט may not be written on
a hide treated with salt and flour but not gallnuts

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר כּוּ׳:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says, etc.:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַסִּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Asi said in the name of Ulla,
There are three kinds of hides:
Matza, ḥifa, and diftera.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the tree discussion and returns to explain a phrase in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hides come in three stages: מצה, חיפה, and דיפתרא.

steps.title: Defining מצה: completely raw hide
steps.stepSummary: מצה means a hide that has not been salted, floured, or treated with gallnuts.
steps.simpleTranslation: מצה means just what it sounds like: hide that is not salted, not floured, and not treated with gallnuts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines the first stage, מצה. It is hide with nothing done to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name מצה means 'plain', like unleavened bread that has nothing added. The three processes that are missing here (salt, flour, gallnuts) are the steps of tanning.

keyTerms.meaning: as it sounds; its plain meaning

steps.confusionAlert: מצה here is not the bread of פסח. It is a word for raw, unprocessed hide.

phrases.english: Matza is as it sounds,
phrases.notes: Just as מצה bread is plain with nothing added, this hide is plain with nothing done to it.

phrases.english: that is not salted and not treated with flour
and not treated with gallnuts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first item in עולא's list.

steps.title: Which הלכה needs this term?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the category מצה matters in הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what הלכה is this needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we need a special name for raw hide. Which law depends on it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A term in the גמרא usually matters because some law depends on it. The question looks for that law.

phrases.english: For what halacha?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks where the definition from step 23 is used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law depends on the category מצה.

steps.title: It matters for carrying on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The size of מצה matters for the law of carrying from one domain to another on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: For carrying out on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the category matters for הוצאה on שבת, carrying an item from one domain to another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person is only liable for carrying on שבת if the item is a minimum useful size. Each type of hide has its own minimum, so we need to know which stage this hide is at.

keyTerms.meaning: carrying an item from one domain to another on שבת

phrases.english: For carrying out on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The term matters for the minimum size that makes one liable for carrying on שבת.

steps.title: How big must it be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the minimum size of מצה that makes one liable for carrying it on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is its minimum size?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the law, the גמרא asks for the exact minimum size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for carrying depends on a set size, called a שיעור. The גמרא wants that size for raw hide.

keyTerms.meaning: minimum size or amount that הלכה requires

phrases.english: And how much is its minimum size?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 25 by asking for the exact measure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum size of מצה for liability on שבת.

steps.title: Enough to wrap a small weight
steps.stepSummary: Based on a teaching of רב שמואל בר יהודה, the measure is enough hide to wrap around a small weight.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב שמואל בר יהודה taught: enough to wrap a small weight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a teaching: the minimum is a piece big enough to wrap a small weight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raw hide is not good for much, but people used it to wrap small weights. Since that is a real use, a piece that size counts on שבת.

phrases.english: As Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda teaches:
Enough to wrap a small weight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The minimum is enough raw hide to wrap a small weight.

steps.title: How small is a small weight?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact size of the 'small weight'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is that?
steps.whatsHappening: 'A small weight' is still unclear, so the גמרא asks exactly how small it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a fixed size for the weight, the measure from step 27 cannot be used in practice.

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for more detail about the measure in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact size of the 'small weight'.

steps.title: אביי: a quarter of a quarter by the פומבדיתא standard
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the small weight is a quarter of a quarter, using the weights of פומבדיתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Like a quarter of a quarter of פומבדיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the exact size: a weight that is one quarter of a quarter, using the measuring system of פומבדיתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the chain: the size of מצה depends on the weight it wraps, and אביי now fixes that weight. One quarter of a quarter is one sixteenth of the full unit.

keyTerms.meaning: פומבדיתא, a major Babylonian town with its own system of weights

steps.whatToRemember: מצה is completely raw hide. On שבת, one is liable for carrying a piece big enough to wrap a small weight, which אביי says is a quarter of a quarter by the weights of פומבדיתא.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Like a quarter of a quarter of Pumbedita.
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't name the unit, but it means a quarter of a quarter of the standard weight used in פומבדיתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כִּי רִיבְעָא דְרִיבְעָא דְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 and finishes the definition of מצה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The small weight is a quarter of a quarter by the measuring system of פומבדיתא.

steps.title: Defining חיפה: salted hide only
steps.stepSummary: חיפה is hide that has been salted, but not treated with flour and not treated with gallnuts.
steps.simpleTranslation: חיפה is hide that has been salted, but not treated with flour and not treated with gallnuts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next stage of leather after מצה and defines חיפה. It has been salted, and that is all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leather is processed in steps: salting, then flour, then gallnuts. מצה has none of these steps. חיפה has only the first one, salt.

keyTerms.meaning: Hide that has been salted only
Treated with gallnuts (the final tanning step)

phrases.english: Ḥifa is hide that is salted,
and not treated with flour, and not treated with gallnuts.
phrases.notes: Gallnuts are a plant growth used in tanning. Treating hide with them is what finishes it into full leather.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from מצה (raw hide) to the next stage of processing in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חיפה = salted, without flour and without gallnuts.

steps.title: Where does חיפה matter in הלכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which law needs this category of hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law do we need to know about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we need a separate name for חיפה. Where does this kind of hide show up in הלכה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A definition only matters if some law depends on it. So the גמרא looks for the practical place where חיפה has its own rule.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? (Where does this matter in practice?)

phrases.english: For what halakha was this mentioned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what practical use there is for the definition just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law depends on the category of חיפה.

steps.title: It matters for carrying on שבת
steps.stepSummary: חיפה matters for the law of carrying from one domain to another on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: For carrying out on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that חיפה has its own rule for הוצאה, carrying from one domain to another on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each type of hide has its own minimum size before carrying it on שבת makes a person liable. So the category matters for setting that size.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying from one domain to another on שבת

phrases.english: For carrying out on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31, using the same answer as for מצה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The law of הוצאה on שבת.

steps.title: What is the size measure for חיפה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the minimum amount of חיפה that makes one liable for carrying it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is its measure?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know חיפה matters for carrying on שבת, the גמרא asks what amount of it a person must carry to be liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, a person is only liable for carrying an amount that is useful. The גמרא wants that useful amount for this kind of hide.

keyTerms.meaning: Measure; the minimum amount that counts in הלכה

phrases.english: And how much is its measure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer to ask for the exact minimum size.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum amount of חיפה for liability in carrying.

steps.title: Enough to make an amulet
steps.stepSummary: Based on a משנה, the measure is enough hide to make a קמיע (amulet).
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: hide, enough to make an amulet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה: for hide, a person is liable once he carries enough to make a קמיע. That is the measure for חיפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salted hide is good enough for small uses like a קמיע, so that use sets its size for carrying on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Amulet; a small written charm, often wrapped in leather

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in שבת 78b.

phrases.english: Hide: enough to make an amulet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the size question by quoting a משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Enough hide to make a קמיע.

steps.title: Defining דיפתרא: salted and floured hide
steps.stepSummary: דיפתרא is hide that has been salted and treated with flour, but not treated with gallnuts.
steps.simpleTranslation: דיפתרא is hide that is salted and treated with flour, but not treated with gallnuts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines the next stage, דיפתרא. It is one step further along than חיפה because it has also been treated with flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דיפתרא is the word the משנה uses for unfinished leather. It has two of the three steps (salt and flour) but is missing the last step (gallnuts).

keyTerms.meaning: Hide that has been salted and treated with flour, but is not fully tanned

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two: חיפה = salt only. דיפתרא = salt plus flour. Neither one has had gallnuts.

phrases.english: Diftera is hide that is salted and treated with flour,
and not treated with gallnuts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next stage of processing after חיפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דיפתרא = salted and floured, without gallnuts.

steps.title: Where does דיפתרא matter in הלכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again asks which law needs this category.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law do we need to know about this?
steps.whatsHappening: Same pattern as before: the גמרא asks where דיפתרא has its own rule in הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא repeats its question for each type of hide, to show that every stage has its own practical meaning.

phrases.english: For what halakha was this mentioned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the question pattern of step 31, now for דיפתרא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law depends on the category of דיפתרא.

steps.title: Also for carrying on שבת
steps.stepSummary: דיפתרא also matters for the law of carrying on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: For carrying out on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is the same: דיפתרא matters for הוצאה on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since דיפתרא is more processed, it is useful for different things than חיפה. That is why it gets its own size measure.

phrases.english: For carrying out on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 36 the same way step 32 answered step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The law of הוצאה on שבת.

steps.title: What is the size measure for דיפתרא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the minimum amount of דיפתרא that makes one liable for carrying it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is its measure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how much דיפתרא a person must carry on שבת to be liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same question as step 33. We expect a different answer, because דיפתרא can be used for different things.

phrases.english: And how much is its measure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up to ask for the exact size.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum amount of דיפתרא for liability in carrying.

steps.title: Enough to write a גט on
steps.stepSummary: The measure for דיפתרא is enough to write a גט on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Enough to write a גט on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the measure is the amount of space needed to write a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דיפתרא is good enough to write on, so its size is set by a writing use, a גט. This shows that people really did write on דיפתרא, which ties back to our משנה about writing a גט on it.
steps.whatToRemember: The order of hide types: מצה (raw) → חיפה (salted, measure: a קמיע) → דיפתרא (salted and floured, measure: a גט) → finished leather (with gallnuts).

phrases.english: Enough to write a bill of divorce on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the size question and finishes the list of hide definitions.

steps.title: Who are the חכמים who say it is valid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's words 'וחכמים מכשירין' and asks who these חכמים are, introducing רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And the חכמים say it is valid.' Who are these חכמים? רבי אלעזר said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and asks which Sage stands behind the opinion of the חכמים. This sets up רבי אלעזר's answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חכמים' is an unnamed group, so the גמרא wants to know which specific Sage holds this view. רבי אלעזר is introduced here, and his actual answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Who are the חכמים? (Which Sage holds this view?)
An אמורא who answers the question

phrases.english: The mishna said: And the Rabbis deem it valid.
Who are these Rabbis?
Rabbi Elazar said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the definitions of hide and returns to the משנה to open a new question about who holds the view of the חכמים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the unnamed חכמים who rule the גט valid.
